They see the bridge. The deck, the water below.
Nobody sees what holds it up. It is under the water.
To check it, someone goes down and looks. By hand.
In water you cannot see through. You feel the stone before you find the crack.
In Massachusetts, 778 bridges need that dive.
And when a flood scours the riverbed, exactly when it matters, nobody can dive. Above about 3 feet per second, divers lose mobility.
The rule is clear. Divers stay. Sonar only supplements the dive.
So we asked a different question. A robot goes first, divers only where the map says.
We built it in one day, in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, a robotics simulator with real-time ray tracing and physics. A digital twin of this crossing, real ArduPilot autopilots flying both robots.
Meet the drone. A spinning laser, 128 beams, builds the bridge as millions of 3D points.
A gimbal camera is the inspector's eyes. Cracks, spalls, stains.
A thermal camera reads temperature. Failing stone runs cooler than sound stone.
Floodlights for the dark underside. GPS for position in open sky.
Meet the ROV. Underwater there is no GPS.
A Doppler velocity log bounces four beams off the bed to navigate. Drift, about 0.4 meters after 60 meters.
A multibeam sonar sees by sound, where a camera sees only mud. A low-light camera confirms it.
8 thrusters hold it still against the current.
The mission. The drone flies the wall.
Under the deck, its GPS fades. 12 satellites drop to 7.
At the water line it spots damage. It hands off the spot.
The ROV dives. Straight to the mark.
Its sonar finds what no one could see. A missing granite block. A scour pit with exposed piles.
4 flagged. 4 inspected. One 3D model, above the water and below.
The brain was built with Kiro, AWS's agentic coding IDE. Megha built the detection pipeline and dashboard.
A YOLOv8 model finds the defects. Every claim cites a detection. An engineer signs off.
The same tools triage the state. All 5,252 bridges, ranked by risk.
Robot first is about 20 to 30 percent cheaper per bridge. Our estimate, the pilot measures it.
The kit costs 16,448 dollars at list price.
By 15 March 2028, every state must re-code scour in the new federal format. Pilot money already exists.
The next step is a 10-bridge pilot, every robot map checked against a diver.
Robot first. Divers only where the map says.
